preamble: High vowel fricativization turns the close back rounded vowel [u] into a syllabic voiced labiodental fricative [v̩]: the lip constriction of the rounded vowel narrows until it produces labiodental friction and the vowel's own resonance is lost. Faytak documents the change in Kom, a Central Ring (Grassfields Bantu) language of Cameroon, where open-syllable *u is regularly reflected as a syllabic fricative, often with a slight frication-free central offglide; the change accompanies a raising chain in which *o and *ʊ move up toward u.

examples.note: Forms in Faytak (2014): v in the Kom forms is the syllabic fricative [v̩], and the diacritic over it is tone. Neighbouring Babanki has ʉ (m̀-bvʉ́) and Bum keeps u (ā-ŋgʷû).

sources: Faytak, M. (2014). High vowel fricativization and chain shift. UC Berkeley Phonology Lab Annual Report. http://www.linguistics.berkeley.edu/PhonLab/documents/2014/Faytak-HighVowel.pdf
